title: Introduce semantic overlay tokens and elevation choreography for buttons, tables, and charts
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Our current token set treats color, elevation, and radii as flat primitives that are reapplied inconsistently across components. This has led to subtle visual regressions at different densities and poor handoffs for motion. We need a small, pragmatic rework that introduces a layer of semantic overlay tokens (e.g., interactive-accent, surface-muted, chart-grid-ink), a clarified elevation choreography for interactive surfaces, and variable radius rules that interpolate across breakpoints.

Goal: Provide a compact token contract that: (1) gives engineers a small set of semantic tokens for component surfaces and accents; (2) defines per-component elevation choreography and shadow ramps for buttons, tables, and charts; (3) introduces responsive radius tokens with interpolation guidance; (4) documents migration steps and QA checks to avoid cross-product regressions.

Scope: color palette aliases (semantic overlay tokens), revised type recommendations for dense vs. comfortable table states (adjusts small parts of the typography scale), spacing/radius variables for small/medium/large and responsive interpolation rules, and a considered shadow/elevation choreography specifically for: primary/secondary buttons, table rows/headers, and chart layers (grid, foreground series, floating tooltips). This ticket focuses on tokens and design specs — engineering implementation and rollout are dependent tasks (ENG-2218).
acceptance_criteria: A documented set of semantic color tokens (names and example usages) exists in the design system page
Elevation choreography defined with token names and recommended CSS box-shadow values for three density modes
Responsive radius tokens with interpolation guidance and three code samples (CSS variables, JS theme object, and Tailwind mapping)
Migration guide with a table of old -> new token mappings and visual diff checklist
Accessibility checks: contrast ratios for all semantic foreground/background pairs meet WCAG AA for normal text and large text as appropriate
Design review approval recorded and at least one engineering PR linked for each major component category (buttons, tables, charts)
